 Piemonte · Torino Five Aosta Valley lakes to explore in autumn
 By Redazione · November 20, 2026 · ≈ 2 min
 Lakes and walks in the Aosta Valley
 You can enjoy alpine scenery in the Aosta Valley without taking on demanding hikes. Short trails and accessible paths lead to lakes framed by forests and mountain peaks, making them suitable for a stroll, a scenic break or a picnic. Here are five lakes to consider for an autumn outing.
 Lake Brusson
 At around 1,300 metres in the Ayas Valley, Lake Brusson is an artificial reservoir known for its emerald-coloured water. Its shores are suited to a walk or a picnic, and there is also a nearby play area. Swimming is not permitted. Visitors can explore the area around Brusson or plan a longer hike to the Palasinaz lakes, reached from Estoul by a climb of around three hours.
 Lake Gover
 Close to the centre of Gressoney-Saint-Jean in the Lys Valley, Lake Gover sits at approximately 1,380 metres and looks towards the Monte Rosa massif. It is easy to reach and makes a pleasant stop on a walk or a visit to the area’s traditional Walser houses. In the early morning, the mountain peaks reflected in the still water create particularly striking views.
 Lake Maen
 Also known as Lake Ussin, this lake lies in Valtournenche, in the Matterhorn Valley, at around 1,300 metres. A flat path of approximately 900 metres runs along its shore and includes 14 fitness stations. A picnic area and a playground are nearby, making it easy to plan a relaxed outdoor break.
 The area is also associated with the Dézarpa, the traditional return of livestock from the high pastures. Usually held in late September, it brings local produce and music to Valtournenche.
 Lake Beauregard
 In the heart of the Valgrisenche, at about 1,710 metres, this large artificial lake is surrounded by woods, rocky slopes and mountains, with views of the Rutor massif. A mostly flat path follows the shore, offering a way to enjoy the landscape without significant climbs. It is a popular destination for autumn scenery; in winter, snow and ice make suitable equipment, especially footwear, essential.
 Lake Lexert
 In the municipality of Bionaz, in the upper Valpelline, Lake Lexert lies at around 1,555 metres among larch and fir trees. A nearby restaurant and car park make it a convenient option for visitors who want to keep walking to a minimum. Clear water and reflections of the surrounding vegetation complete the alpine setting.
 Practical tips
 Check trail conditions and the weather forecast before setting out.
 Wear suitable footwear even for short walks, particularly in wet or cold conditions.
 Follow local rules and take all rubbish away with you.
 Some lakes are artificial reservoirs and may have access or use restrictions.
